title: S&P's Concern on DSI (May 2026)
original_filename: spglobal.com-Bulletin Execution Risks Lurk In Indonesias Res.pdf
summary: This S&P Global Ratings bulletin highlights the significant execution risks of Indonesia's sudden plan to centralize the export of crude palm oil, coal, and iron alloy through a new state-owned enterprise, Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia. While the government intends to curb improper transfer-pricing and bolster its historically low revenue base—which sits at just 15% of GDP—S&P warns that the abrupt policy and its narrow three-month implementation window could trigger trade disruptions, damage investor confidence, and spark capital outflows. Consequently, if poorly executed, the plan risks disrupting exports and squeezing the country's balance of payments, creating downward uncertainty for Indonesia's current BBB/Stable/A-2 credit rating.

title: Counter Analysis on DSI concern (May 2026)
original_filename: Counter Argument on S&P concerning DSI.pdf
summary: This document presents a robust counter-case to S&P Global Ratings' cautionary bulletin regarding Indonesia’s centralisation of palm oil, coal, and iron alloy exports under the new state-owned enterprise, Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia. While S&P highlights downside risks to Indonesia’s BBB/Stable rating due to potential trade disruptions and weakened investor sentiment from the tight three-month transition window , the counter-argument maintains that these execution concerns are heavily overstated and that the upside scenario is underweighted.
